cases.title: Writes fail while byte capacity looks healthy and application retries amplify load
cases.symptom: A production Linux service begins failing some writes with ENOSPC while the volume still reports substantial free bytes; request latency and CPU then climb as clients and workers retry failed operations.

initial_evidence.summary: Current application logs contain repeated ENOSPC failures for small metadata and temporary-file writes.
The affected filesystem currently reports roughly 38% free byte capacity.
A filesystem dashboard sample from twenty minutes earlier showed unusually high inode utilization.
Application retry rate and request concurrency rose sharply after the first write failures.
An earlier memory-pressure alert cleared before the write failures began.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect current inode consumption and free inode counts on the affected filesystem without changing state.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether namespace capacity is exhausted even though byte capacity remains available.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect the exact failing write paths and filesystem/mount boundaries from current logs and process metadata.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether ENOSPC originates from the expected filesystem rather than a different mount or quota boundary.

diagnostic_actions.description: Read current retry, queue-depth, and concurrency metrics for the affected workers.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether retry behavior is independently amplifying resource pressure after the storage failure begins.

diagnostic_actions.description: Attempt one bounded temporary-file create/unlink in the affected mount using a dedicated test path.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Test current namespace allocation behavior without broad cleanup or service restart.

diagnostic_actions.description: Recursively delete the service log tree to free filesystem objects immediately.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Attempt emergency capacity recovery without first proving ownership, retention, or rollback safety.

diagnostic_actions.description: Restart every application worker to clear the retry storm before isolating the filesystem condition.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Attempt broad load reset without resolving the write failure or proving restart safety.

cases.title: Service discovery and cross-node pod connectivity degrade at the same time
cases.symptom: After a node-pool and CNI rollout, some pods intermittently fail service-name resolution while a separate subset can resolve names but cannot complete cross-node connections; same-node traffic is mostly healthy.

initial_evidence.summary: A same-node pod-to-pod connection succeeds repeatedly on an affected worker node.
Cross-node connection attempts show repeated transport retransmission candidates before application timeout.
Several DNS service pods restarted around the incident window and some affected clients report lookup timeouts.
The CNI health dashboard reports green, but its most recent sample predates the rollout by fifteen minutes.
The node-pool image and CNI configuration were rolled out in the same maintenance window.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect current pod routes, tunnel state, and node-to-node forwarding entries on affected and healthy nodes.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether cross-node forwarding state diverged after the rollout.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect current DNS service endpoints, readiness, restart history, and client resolver configuration.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether service-discovery failures form a separate fault path from cross-node forwarding.

diagnostic_actions.description: Collect a bounded metadata-only packet trace for one failing cross-node flow and one failing DNS lookup.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Separate transport-path loss from resolver behavior without retaining arbitrary payloads.

diagnostic_actions.description: Run a bounded connectivity probe matrix between one affected pod, one healthy pod, and the DNS service.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Discriminate node-local, cross-node, and DNS failure boundaries with a small active probe set.

diagnostic_actions.description: Restart every cluster DNS pod immediately.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Attempt to reset one visible symptom before establishing whether networking has an independent failure.

diagnostic_actions.description: Remove cluster network policies to eliminate possible filtering during diagnosis.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Bypass segmentation controls instead of isolating the failed forwarding or DNS path.

cases.title: Signed cloud requests and authorization checks fail for different reasons after a deployment
cases.symptom: After a workload deployment, one host receives request-signature time errors while a separate serverless component using the same role family receives authorization denials on a newly used API operation.

initial_evidence.summary: Current API errors from one host state that request timestamps fall outside the accepted signing window.
A newly deployed function receives AccessDenied for one API action while other actions under the same identity succeed.
The affected function resolves to the expected role identity and account, but the policy set changed in the deployment window.
A cached policy-simulation result from before deployment shows the new action as allowed.
The host time-service configuration differs from the current fleet baseline, but no current offset measurement is yet available.

diagnostic_actions.description: Measure the host's current time offset against an independent trusted time source without adjusting the clock.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether signature rejection is consistent with current clock error.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect the function's currently effective role, boundaries, session policy, and resource policy for the denied action.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether authorization denial is independent of the host signature failure.

diagnostic_actions.description: Run a non-mutating authorization simulation against the current policy generation for the exact denied action and resource.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Replace stale policy evidence with a current decision trace.

diagnostic_actions.description: Issue one bounded read-only signed health request from the affected host after recording its current clock offset.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Test whether request-signing validity changes independently of IAM authorization behavior.

diagnostic_actions.description: Attach a broad administrator policy to the workload role to eliminate authorization denials during diagnosis.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Bypass least privilege rather than identify the exact policy or signing fault.

diagnostic_actions.description: Rotate credentials across the workload fleet before determining whether credential material is implicated.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Perform a broad identity change unrelated to one or both observed failure paths.

cases.title: TLS validation failures coexist with stale reads on a replicated database service
cases.symptom: Some strict clients reject TLS when connecting through one database endpoint while clients that connect successfully report increasingly stale reads from a replica pool.

initial_evidence.summary: Strict clients terminate the handshake during certificate validation on one database endpoint.
The visible leaf certificate on that endpoint is within its validity interval.
Current replication telemetry shows one read replica falling progressively behind its upstream source.
The service dashboard still reports healthy because its certificate and replication panels last refreshed before the incident window.
The primary database reports normal transaction latency and no corresponding write backlog.

diagnostic_actions.description: Validate the complete certificate chain served by the failing endpoint against current trust anchors and time.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether TLS failure originates beyond the apparently-valid leaf certificate.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect current receive/replay positions, queue depth, and replication errors for each read replica.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether stale reads are caused by an independent replication fault and localize the lagging member.

diagnostic_actions.description: Compare served certificate-chain digests and endpoint configuration across healthy and failing database listeners.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Identify endpoint-specific TLS material drift without modifying service configuration.

diagnostic_actions.description: Issue bounded read-only consistency probes to the primary and each replica using a dedicated test record/version marker.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Measure current replica visibility without initiating failover or writes outside the test fixture.

diagnostic_actions.description: Force a database failover to move traffic away from the lagging replica pool before isolating TLS state.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Attempt topology recovery with significant availability impact before proving it addresses both failures.

diagnostic_actions.description: Disable certificate validation on clients to restore database connectivity.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Bypass transport authenticity rather than repair the endpoint chain.
